extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent agents filing or prosecuting patent applications in Singapore
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural requirements and formalities for Singapore patent applications, including inventor mention, priority claims, missing parts (drawings/description), and the specific forms/timelines the Registry reviews and enforces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to be mentioned as inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is granted primarily to the inventor(s). The inventor(s) have a right to be mentioned in any patent and published application for the invention unless another person is entitled by law, treaty, international convention, or agreement entered into before the making of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to identify inventor on application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant is not the sole inventor, the inventor(s) may be identified by filling Parts 3.3 and 3.4 of the Applicant & Inventor Details tab of Patents Form 1, or by filing Patents Form 8 to identify inventor(s) and derivation of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PCT national phase entries, inventorship declared in the PCT application means a separate Form 8 is not required (but duplicate records may occur if filed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines to file Patents Form 8 (Normal application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents Form 8 must be filed within 16 months from the declared priority date, or if there is no priority date, from its date of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule references: Rule 18(1), 28(f), 86(8) & 86(8A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines to file Patents Form 8 (Divisional application)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a divisional application, Patents Form 8 must be filed within 16 months from the declared priority date (or filing date if none), or on the initiation date of the divisional application (Patents Form 1), whichever is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines to file Patents Form 8 (PCT national phase entry)
rubrics_metrics.description: For PCT applications entering national phase in Singapore, Patents Form 8 must be filed within 16 months from the declared priority date (or filing date if none), or within 2 months from the date national phase begins, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National phase entry begins when early national phase entry is requested and requirements satisfied, or at expiry of 30 months or extended time period for normal/late entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer review checklist for Form 8
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of Patents Form 8, the Formalities officer will review: (a) the form is filed within the specified timelines or extension approved; (b) at least one inventor is named; (c) derivation of rights is indicated (Part 6); (d) representation details and/or address for service on the form correspond with records (otherwise Form CM1 or CM2 is required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any requirement not met, the officer will invite clarification/rectification within 2 months; remedies include filing Form CM4 for corrections, or CM1/CM2 to update representation/address; replies may be submitted via eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification process and timeframe for Form 8 deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: If Form 8 requirements are not met, the Formalities officer will send a letter inviting the applicant to clarify or rectify within 2 months from the letter date; if not rectified, a reminder is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To rectify errors on the form, file Form CM4 and indicate relevant rule (Rules 58 and/or 91). To update representation/address (not a correction of error), file CM1 or CM2. Submit clarification letters via eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if Form 8 not complied with
rubrics_metrics.description: If objections cannot be overcome or there is no response, the request will be refused and the applicant notified. If the time for filing Patents Form 8 has passed, the application will be treated as abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome when Form 8 is approved
rubrics_metrics.description: If all requirements are met, the Formalities officer will approve the request and notify applicant(s) and inventor(s); an entry is made in the register and in the next Patents Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Patents Form 7 to add or remove inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: A person alleging they ought to have been mentioned as inventor may file Patents Form 7 to add themselves; to allege someone ought not to have been mentioned, file Form 7 to remove that inventor. A single Form 7 may be used to both add and remove where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents Form 7 must be filed together with a statement setting out fully the facts relied upon for the addition/removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer review checklist for Form 7
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of Form 7 the officer will check: (a) fee paid; (b) for addition, request filed by inventor to be added; (c) for removal, request filed by person other than inventor to be removed; (d) inventor is an individual; (e) a statement of fact covering all inventors is filed; (f) a declaration that a copy was served on the other party at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements not met, officer invites clarification within 2 months; rectify errors via Form CM4 (selecting appropriate correction option). Update representation/address via CM1/CM2. Clarifications and supporting documents may be submitted via eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal or approval process for Form 7 requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If objections cannot be overcome or no response, the Formalities officer will refuse the request. If the application is in order, the officer will send a copy of the application to all applicants and inventors on record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to addition/removal of inventors (Form 58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any recipient of copies of the application may oppose the application by filing Patents Form 58 within 2 months from the date of the notice; the request should be accompanied by a statement setting out the grounds of opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address notification and effect on opposition period
rubrics_metrics.description: If mail is returned due to invalid addresses, the Formalities officer will write to the patent agent or address for service on record to request an updated address for the affected party. The time for opposition for that affected party will be calculated from the date the notification is sent to the updated address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure applicant and inventor addresses are updated so addition/removal can be timely effected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes of opposition proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the outcome of the opposition is successful, the Formalities officer will refuse the request. If the opposition is unsuccessful or none is received within 2 months from notification, the officer will update the register and notify the requestor and affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of errors in list of inventors (Form 8 vs CM4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For errors in the list of inventors, addition or removal may be done by filing a fresh Patents Form 8 if still within the allowable time period. Otherwise, file Form CM4 together with supporting documents to show there is an error; a simple declaration is insufficient—detailed explanation of how the error occurred is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Correction of Form lodged' for errors on the form; 'Correction of Specification...' for errors on the description; 'Correction of any other document...' for other documents (see Chapter 11.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing sequence of inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: For change in the sequence of inventors, the applicant may write via eCommunications and the Formalities officer will update records accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of inventors due to specification amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Removal of inventors due to amendments of the specification requires a written request and letter of consent from all applicants and inventors submitted via eCommunications to update the register; if consent is not given by all parties, the officer will inform the applicant to request written consent or resolve by filing Patents Form 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: General priority filing rule (12 month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must file his Singapore patent application within 12 months from the date of filing of the earlier relevant application; where there are multiple earlier applications, the 12 months is counted from the earliest relevant application. The priority date will be the date of filing of that earlier relevant application (or the earliest of them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration of priority must be made by the applicant at the time of filing the Singapore patent application (subject to exceptions described below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition or change of priority via Patents Form 57 (Rule 9(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration claiming priority to an earlier relevant application may be made after filing and cause the application to have a declared priority date or bring forward the declared priority date if: (a) the declared priority date to be claimed is not more than 12 months before the date of filing of the application in suit; (b) the declaration is made on Patents Form 57 within 16 months (not extendable) from the declared priority date for normal applications (or on filing date for divisionals); and (c) the application has not been published under Section 27 (any early publication request must be withdrawn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to use Form 57 where Rule 9 applies cannot be corrected by Form CM4 (Rule 91). Examples in the manual illustrate correct vs incorrect use of Form 57 vs CM4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of mistake in priority declaration that changes declared priority date (Rule 9(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A correction to a priority declaration that would change the declared priority date to a different date may be made on Patents Form 57 within 16 months (not extendable) from the declared priority date (or on same day for divisionals), provided the application has not been published under Section 27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of Form CM4 is not permitted where Rule 9(3) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late declaration of priority (restoration; Rule 9A)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to file a declaration of priority later than 12 months but no later than 14 months from the declared priority date may be made on Patents Form 57 within 14 months (not extendable): (i) from declared priority date for normal applications; (ii) on same day as filing for divisionals; or (iii) within 1 month from national phase begin for national phase entry applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the applicant failed to file within 12 months, the request must indicate whether the failure occurred despite due care or was unintentional. The application must not have been published under Section 27. Rule 9A applies; correction under Rule 91 (Form CM4) is not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined addition/change of priority and late declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: If a declaration of priority is made more than 12 months but not more than 14 months earlier than the filing date, the applicant should request to make a late declaration at the same time as making the declaration of priority; a late declaration may only be made if the earlier application has been declared in accordance with Rule 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 'intended' earlier application was not declared when filing the application in suit, priority to that application cannot be claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction causing declared priority to fall into 12–14 month window
rubrics_metrics.description: If a correction of a declared priority date will result in the declared priority date being more than 12 months but not more than 14 months earlier than the filing date, the applicant should request a late declaration of priority (Rule 9A) at the same time as correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer review checklist for priority requests (Form 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of a priority-related request (e.g., Form 57), the officer will check: (a) fee paid; (b) not a Patents Form 1 application having a date of filing before 1 Apr 2007; (c) national application has not been published under Section 27 (for non-PCT national phase entries); (d) no pending request for early publication (Form 9); (e) representation details/address for service correspond with record (else CM1/CM2); (f) for late priority, reason for failure indicated in Part 6 of the form; (g) form filed within time; (h) declaration states the date of filing of the earlier application and the country filed in; (i) priority application/file number or priority documents may be filed within 16 months from declared priority date; and (j) priority details indicated correspond with option selected and match records where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time: multiple extensions up to 6 months for providing details/documents may be requested on Patents Form 45 before end of the 6-month period; further extension beyond 6 months possible if requested no later than 6 months after expiry of first period and accompanied by a Statutory Declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification, refusal or approval process for priority requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If priority-request requirements are not met, the Formalities officer will invite clarification/rectification within 2 months; if not overcome or no response, the request will be refused and entered in the register. If the request satisfies requirements, the officer will approve, notify the applicant, update pre-grant due dates and enter the event in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rectifications may be effected via Form CM4, CM1/CM2, or eCommunications as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing missing drawings or part of description (Patents Form 56 eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications initiated on or after 1 Apr 2007, a drawing or part of the description missing from the application may be submitted by filing Patents Form 56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of filing of the application will be changed to the submission date of the missing part unless the applicant requests the date of filing remain unchanged; if requirements are not met the earlier accorded date may be re-dated to a later date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire description missing is not a 'missing part'
rubrics_metrics.description: When the entire description is missing, it will not be considered a missing part and a deficiency will be issued. The description may be submitted via eCommunications and the date of filing will be accorded when the description is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to request 'later date of filing not to apply' when filing a missing part
rubrics_metrics.description: To request that a later date of filing not apply (i.e., retain original filing date) when filing a missing part, the following must be met: (a) Patents Form 56 filed within 3 months (not extendable) from date of filing or initiation date for divisionals; (b) a reference to an earlier application declared in accordance with Section 17(2); (c) a statement that the description is incorporated in the application by reference to, and is completely contained in, the earlier application as filed; (d) furnishing of information in relation to the earlier relevant application; and (e) filing of documents in relation to the earlier relevant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the earlier application or English translation need not be furnished if it had previously been filed at the Registry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination notification and missing part remedy timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If during preliminary examination the Formalities officer finds a drawing referred to in the description or a part of the description missing, the applicant must be formally notified in the Preliminary Examination report. To request the later date of filing not to apply, Patents Form 56 must be filed within 3 months (not extendable) from the date of the Registrar's notification, together with the other requirements (reference, incorporation statement, information and documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same documentation rules as filing without prior notification (see above).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing missing part must be contemporaneous with request to retain filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Although filing a missing part and requesting that the original date of filing be retained can be made within 3 months from the relevant date, the request must be made at the same time as the filing of the missing part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing restriction relative to search/examination requests (apps on/after 14 Feb 2014)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications lodged on or after 14 Feb 2014, the missing part must be filed with Patents Form 56 before the applicant files a request for a search report, search and examination report, examination report, or supplementary examination report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 26A(1)(b) and related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of description by reference to earlier application
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications initiated on or after 1 Apr 2007, instead of filing the description on filing date, an applicant may obtain a date of filing by: (a) declaring a priority date/reference to an earlier relevant application (Section 17(2)); (b) providing the date of filing of that earlier application and the country it was filed in; and (c) making a statement that the description is incorporated in the application by reference to, and is completely contained in, the earlier application as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to file required documents for incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant does not file required documents within 3 months from the date of filing, the application will be treated as abandoned. Required documents include: (a) a written notice confirming incorporation by reference; (b) the description; (c) Patents Form 56; and (d) a copy of the earlier application and its English translation if any (note only the latter requirement is extendable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for earlier relevant application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the earlier relevant application is not in English, an English translation of those parts of that document in which the missing part of the Singapore patent application is contained must be filed with the Registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 26A(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer review checklist for Form 56 requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a missing-part request (Form 56), the Formalities officer will check: (a) application is a non-PCT national phase entry application lodged on or after 1 Apr 2007; (b) the application is not withdrawn or granted; (c) the priority application indicated corresponds with Patents Form 1 or records; (d) a description is enclosed if the description or part of the description is missing; (e) representation details/address for service correspond with record (otherwise CM1/CM2); (f) the form is filed within the timelines set out above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements not met, officer will invite clarification within 2 months; rectify via CM4, CM1/CM2, or eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval, refusal, and examination consequences for missing-part filings
rubrics_metrics.description: If objections cannot be overcome or there is no response within the time period, the Formalities officer will refuse the request and notify the applicant; preliminary examination will not be performed on the missing part. If the request satisfies all requirements, the officer will approve the request and preliminary examination will be performed on the missing part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of filed missing part (Form 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a missing part (Patents Form 56) is filed, it may be withdrawn as long as the prescribed period for doing so has not expired. Withdrawal may only be effected by written notice via eCommunications within the prescribed time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the withdrawal request is in order, the Formalities officer will approve and send an approval letter. If not in order, the officer will invite clarification within 2 months. If the applicant fails to comply and does not withdraw before the prescribed period ends, the missing parts will be treated as included in the application and the date of filing will be changed to the date the missing parts were filed.
